In April 2022, months after retaking power, the Taliban banned the growing of opium poppy across Afghanistan. Poppy fields shrank by more than nine tenths in 2023.

Afghanistan had long been the source of most of the world's illegal heroin. Poppy grows well in dry provinces such as Helmand, needs little water and earns far more than wheat, so many farm families depended on it. Twenty years of foreign aid and eradication campaigns after 2001 had failed to stop it.

The Taliban had done the same once before. Their ban of 2000 also cut the harvest sharply, before their fall in 2001 let the crop return. This time the ban held for several seasons. It hit rural incomes hard in an economy already in crisis, pushed some farmers to migrate and shifted part of the drug trade toward synthetic drugs such as methamphetamine.
sum: In April 2022, months after retaking power, the Taliban banned the growing of opium poppy across Afghanistan. Poppy fields shrank by more than nine tenths in 2023.
